newsitem.title: KENYA: ICRC steps up emergency aid to eastern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: ICRC steps up emergency aid to eastern Zaire.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) flew medical equipment and material to eastern Zaire on Sunday to help thousands suffering because of conflict in the region.
The ICRC said a C-130 Hercules transport plane flew from Nairobi, Kenya, to Goma, Zaire, loaded with equipment to upgrade the hospital in the town of Uvira in southern Kivu province.
It said in a statement medical facilities in Uvira were under increasing strain because of inter-ethnic fighting and an influx of war wounded from neighbouring Burundi to the east.

It said the supplies flown in were provided by the German Red Cross, which also sent a five-member surgical team to reinforce the casualty unit at Uvira hospital while the Belgian Red Cross would support its public health operations.

"A survey in north Kivu has revealed that many medical centres have been abandoned, looted or damaged during the ethnic conflict in the area," it added. "Under the new ICRC initiative six hospitals and 30 health centres will receive support."
The Geneva-based ICRC launched an urgent appeal last Wednesday for $11 million to fund the expanded aid operation.

The Zairean army is in conflict with Tutsis from the Banyamulenge ethnic group in southern Kivu and refugees from Burundi are also crossing into Zaire to escape a civil war between the Tutsi-dominated Burundian army and Hutu rebels.
Human rights watchdog Amnesty International late last month accused Zairean troops and officials of atrocities against Banyamulenge civilians in eastern Zaire over the past month.
The Zairean government says Banyamulenge Tutsis who had left Zaire had recently infiltrated back from Rwanda and killed dozens of Zaireans in the east since the start of September.
